verification_methodology_note: Anti-Narcotics and Psychotropic Substances Control Law «نظام مكافحة المخدرات والمؤثرات العقلية» — Royal Decree M/39 dated 8/7/1426H (13 August 2005 CE), approving Council of Ministers Resolution No. 152 (12/6/1426H), which itself followed Shura Council Resolution No. 51/50 (7/11/1425H). Issued by King Abdullah bin Abdulaziz Al Saud. Article 73 repeals the prior narcotics-trafficking prevention system issued by Supreme Order No. 3318, dated 9/4/1353H. PRIMARY SOURCE: the official Bureau of Experts portal (laws.boe.gov.sa) — direct WebFetch failed (HTTP 503) on both the LawDetails and Viewer URLs, but the r.jina.ai proxy successfully retrieved the complete Markdown-converted page, including the Royal Decree preamble, the Council of Ministers Resolution text, and all 74 articles verbatim. This became the primary extracted text and is the reading used wherever primary sources diverge (see known_unresolved_discrepancies). CROSS-VERIFICATION: the BOE text was checked word-for-word, article by article, against nezams.com (independent Arabic legal-reference aggregator, fetched via r.jina.ai raw HTML, not LLM-summarized) — full agreement across all 74 articles except one textual variant in Article 42, paragraph 1 (documented below). A third independent source, qadha.org.sa's published reference book ("نظام مكافحة المخدرات والمؤثرات العقلية ولائحته التنفيذية مع الفهارس" by عبدالرحمن بن فالح بن محمود الدوسري, Riyadh 1445H, published under الجمعية العلمية القضائية السعودية "قضاء", ISBN 978-603-92112-4-2), was fetched as a PDF and extracted with pdftotext; the highest-stakes penalty articles (37, the death-penalty article, plus 38, 39, 40, and 49 — key penalty amounts of 1,000-300,000 SAR fines, 6 months-25+ years imprisonment, up to 50 lashes) were triple-verified against it and matched exactly. Every one of the 74 articles rests on at least two independently-sourced full-text copies (BOE + nezams.com); the penalty articles rest on three. A Wayback Machine cross-check could not be completed — the archive.org 'available' API confirmed a January 2026 snapshot exists, but retrieving its content failed via every method attempted (direct curl blocked by sandbox egress policy, WebFetch refused web.archive.org, and the r.jina.ai proxy became rate-limited/IP-blocked after repeated calls) — this is a documented methodology gap, mitigated by the two other independently -sourced full-text matches. NO formal الباب (Part) / الفصل (Chapter) structure exists in this law — confirmed by a full-text grep of the qadha.org.sa combined law+regulation reference PDF, which returned zero instances of 'الباب' or 'الفصل' used as structural markers; the law instead uses unnumbered topical headers interspersed among its 74 sequential articles (see chapter_structure, which models these headers without inventing باب/فصل labels). One AI-generated web-search summary asserted a 'الباب الثاني'/'الفصل الأول' division; this could not be substantiated against any of the three primary sources and is flagged as unverified/likely erroneous, not modeled. AMENDMENT STATUS: no Royal Decree or Council of Ministers Resolution amending the 74 articles of M/39 itself was found; nezams.com's own metadata states 'no amendments to date', and the 2024-published qadha.org.sa reference book reproduces the identical, unamended 74-article text. This conclusion rests on convergent negative evidence rather than a definitive official 'amendment log' (no such feature was accessible on BOE) — a residual verification gap, documented below. Article 70 grants the Minister of Health delegated authority to amend the annexed substance schedules (الجداول 1-4) by administrative decision; pursuant to this, Administrative Decision No. 13362/ق (28/5/1444H, amended 29/8/1444H) restructured the schedule categories. This is a schedule update, not a textual amendment to any of the 74 articles, and no article is marked معدلة. An Implementing Regulation (اللائحة التنفيذية) exists — Council of Ministers Resolution No. 201, dated 10/6/1431H (24 May 2010) — corroborated across 4 independent sources (qistas.com, moi.gov.sa, moh.gov.sa, BOE search snippets) but not independently verified to the verbatim-text standard applied to the main law, and not extracted in this track — candidate for a follow-up companion-track ingestion.

known_unresolved_discrepancies.description: Textual variant, Article 42, paragraph 1: the BOE text (via r.jina.ai) reads "لا تقام الدعوى بسبب تعاطي..." (no lawsuit/case shall be brought), which is legally coherent. nezams.com's independent extraction instead reads "لا تقام الدعوة بسبب تعاطي..." ("no invitation shall be brought" — nonsensical), almost certainly an OCR/typo error on nezams.com's side. The BOE (official government source) reading, "الدعوى," was adopted as authoritative in this track's article text — flagged explicitly here rather than silently corrected.

Grammatical irregularity in the official text itself, Article 35's header: both BOE and nezams.com identically render the heading as "المادة الخامسة الثلاثون" — omitting the conjunctive "و" (and) used consistently in every other analogous ordinal (e.g. "الحادية والعشرون," "السادسة والثلاثون," "الحادية والأربعون"). Because this appears identically in two independently-sourced copies of the official text, it does not look like a transcription artifact of either aggregator, though a shared upstream OCR/rendering source cannot be fully ruled out. Preserved verbatim as found in number_label_ar — NOT silently corrected to "الخامسة والثلاثون".

No formal الباب (Part) / الفصل (Chapter) numbering exists in this law — only unnumbered topical headers interspersed among the 74 articles, confirmed by a full-text grep of the qadha.org.sa combined law+regulation reference PDF (zero instances of 'الباب' or 'الفصل' as structural markers). One AI-generated web-search summary asserted the law is divided into 'الباب الثاني' with 'الفصل الأول'; this claim was NOT substantiated by direct examination of three independent full-text sources (BOE, nezams.com, qadha.org.sa) and is flagged as likely erroneous or a conflation with a different document/draft. chapter_structure in this track models only the topical headers, without inventing باب/فصل labels.

Wayback Machine cross-check could not be completed due to technical access restrictions: the sandbox's egress policy blocked direct curl access to web.archive.org, WebFetch explicitly refused to fetch web.archive.org, and the r.jina.ai proxy became rate-limited/IP-blocked after repeated use. The archive.org 'wayback/available' API did confirm a January 2026 snapshot exists, but its content was never retrieved. This is a documented methodology gap, mitigated by having two other independently-sourced full-text copies (BOE + nezams.com) that matched almost perfectly.

The 'no amendments since 1426H' conclusion rests on convergent negative evidence (nezams.com's own metadata states 'no amendments to date'; the 2024-published qadha.org.sa reference book reproduces identical, unamended text; targeted searches for an amending instrument found none for this specific law) rather than on a definitive official 'amendment log' — no such version/history registry feature was accessible on the BOE portal (page-2/alternate-view fetch attempts returned 503/422 errors or timed out). Flagged as a residual verification gap, not a confirmed absence of amendments.

Unverified/lower-confidence claims surfaced about amendments to a RELATED BUT SEPARATE instrument — the National Committee for Combating Drugs organizing regulation (تنظيم اللجنة الوطنية لمكافحة المخدرات, a distinct BOE law entry, ID b2c545f0-d65f-4c13-b712-a9a700f193b6) — reportedly amended by Council of Ministers Resolution No. 651 (1/11/1438H, adding the head of General Intelligence and the Director-General of Border Guards to committee membership) and Council of Ministers Resolution No. 211 (11/4/1443H, on committee meeting procedures). These do NOT amend this law's 74 articles (Royal Decree M/39) — they pertain to a different instrument entirely. The claim came only from an AI-generated web-search summary, not from direct primary-source text retrieval, so it is flagged as unverified and out of scope for this track.

Stale-authority note: the law (2005) predates several Saudi institutional reorganizations. Article 68 references "مؤسسة النقد العربي السعودي" — SAMA's pre-2020 name (renamed "البنك المركزي السعودي" in 2020) — as one of the entities whose specialists hold judicial-seizure authority (صفة الضبط الجنائي). Articles 12-27 reference "وزارة الصحة" (Ministry of Health) throughout, even though "الهيئة العامة للغذاء والدواء" (Saudi Food and Drug Authority) now administers much of the practical schedule/licensing regime in practice. Both are preserved verbatim as enacted in the article text — not silently updated to current institution names. Documented here as a real-world regulatory-evolution note for the corpus/build process, not as a textual defect.

An Implementing Regulation (اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام مكافحة المخدرات والمؤثرات العقلية) is confirmed to exist — issued via Council of Ministers Resolution No. 201, dated 10/6/1431H (24 May 2010) — and corroborated across 4 independent sources (qistas.com, moi.gov.sa, moh.gov.sa, and BOE search snippets). However, none of those 4 corroborating sources' PDFs/pages were independently opened and verified beyond WebSearch summaries, so this is only moderate-confidence, sufficient to note the Regulation's existence/date but not to the verbatim-text standard applied to the main law. Not extracted in this track — candidate for a follow-up companion-track ingestion.
